findings.where: Near Tropos horn (bell box 1040,40-1320,240), at 800 px and in the 168 px thumbnail

At site sizes it reads as a play icon on a black panel, not as a yellow acrylic horn. The track-horn1 head aimed at the horn (4.5 W/m2, 12 deg) adds nothing you can see, because clear acrylic does not scatter light. The panel behaves honestly; the problem is how the picture reads.
findings.expected: A horn that reads as the approved lemon horn, lit by something a real bar or photographer could have. It must be something the polished horn can mirror, or be seen against (a lit niche back, a large real softbox on its mirror rays). A reflection-only card does not qualify.

findings.where: Near Tropos woofer cone and dust cap (woofer-cone#1 box 1100,388-1256,547)

Under the same head, the cone (left flank L* 63.2, cap 64.2) outreads the white lining beside the woofer (41.4 and 45.8). In the approved Acid front the cone is dark (14-26 L* against a wall of 89). The head is honest; the trouble is what its hot spot does to the product read. I could not read the cone material's albedo or gloss (the product material files are not in the folder), so I cannot tell whether the model's cone is too light or the head is simply too hot on it.
findings.expected: A dark cone, as in the approved front, with the cabinet still lit. For example, aim the head so its hot spot grazes the cabinet and the cone sits at the pool's edge, or use a larger, softer source.

findings.what: fixed-4 still carries a ray-visibility trick. horn-card is an emitter that exists only in reflections: diffuse 0 (visible_diffuse False, so it lights nothing), specular 1, camera off, shadow off (panel() sets visible_shadow False), transmission off (gen.py), one-sided (back transparent), and ramped 0.25-1-0.25 along x. No real card behaves like that. In fixed-4 I found no visible effect: with the ceiling panel at 0, the near horn is black (bell 0.1, wedge box 0.0), and the Cores look the same as in fixed when zoomed. No frame without the card exists, so its remaining effect elsewhere is unmeasured. Geometry says it can reach the camera only through a final glossy bounce on curved surfaces (Cores, shades, horns), a few pixels at most.
findings.expected: Delete it (fixed-5 = fixed-4 without horn-card; on the measured evidence nothing visible should change). Alternatively, make it a real card or softbox with every ray on (diffuse 1, shadow on, transmission on) and measure what it then lights.
findings.evidence: fixed4.json lights.horn-card = {diffuse 0.0, specular 1.0, transmission false, ramp ...}. lights.py panel(): visible_camera = camera (False), visible_shadow = False, visible_diffuse = d>=1, visible_glossy = s>=1, transmission False -> visible_transmission False. Tiles card0: bell 0.1, wedge 0.0. Crop: critic-lights/cores-zoom.png

findings.where: live frame (the site's tropos-bar.webp): near horn and near cabinet
findings.what: Live's look rests on two tricks. First, the horn's whole glow is the horn card seen through the clear horn: a camera-invisible, diffuse-invisible, shadowless, graduated emitter that lights nothing. Second, the cabinet's inner glow comes from the shadow-ray shortcut on the Tropos materials. These are lights no real place could have, and they change what the picture shows. live.json also leaves filter_glossy at the engine default 0.5 and reflective caustics off.
findings.expected: Replace live with an honest frame.
findings.evidence: live.json horn-card has no transmission key, so it is transmission-visible. Bell L* live 8.9 vs fixed 0.3; 7538 vs 22 px over L* 30. Cabinet front 35.6 vs 15.4 with the shortcut cut (meas.md). live.json render: caustics_reflective false, no filter_glossy key; render.py blur_glossy = R.get('filter_glossy', 0.5)

findings.what: The head's 5 W/m2 is a Lambertian label (area_power: E * pi * d^2) that ignores spread. Narrowing it to 14 deg concentrated the light, so fixed-4 puts more light on the cone than fixed-3's 6 W/m2 at 22 deg, not less. A 14 deg head at 5 lands about where a 22 deg head at 8 would.
findings.expected: Read the head as stronger than its label. If the cone has to come down, measure on the cone, not by the W/m2 label.

found.recommendation: On honesty, fixed-4 can replace live with named exceptions. As a picture it is not ready yet. Before it goes up: (1) delete horn-card, the one remaining ray-visibility trick. With the ceiling panel at 0 the near horn is black either way, so removing it should change nothing visible; a fixed-5 without it would confirm. (2) Hang ceiling-panel fully below the 3.40 ceiling. (3) Bring house and house-left inside the room, for example planet_bar's own 1.6 m house at (6.9, 0.6, 2.3). track-front1, ceiling-panel, the track heads and the two Mantle heads are lights a bar or a location photographer could have, and they behave honestly. Separately from honesty, at 800 px and at the 168 px thumbnail the near Tropos reads as a silver woofer under a black horn with a grey triangle: cone L* 63-64 against 14-26 in the approved Acid front; bell 1.2 against 8.9 live. Fix it with a different honest plan, not a trick. Keep the head's hot spot off the cone. Give the horn something real to mirror or be seen against, such as a lit niche back from the room's own speaker-niche strip (now 0; untested) or a real softbox on its mirror rays with every ray on.
found.summary: I read fixed4.json, lights.py, render.py and planet_bar.py, and measured live, fixed, fixed-3, fixed-4 and the README's crop tiles. I located the tiles in the frame (box 960,0-1536,631 at 0.75; mean error 1.46 levels) and used them to separate the panel's effect (card 0/6/15) from the head's (4 vs 6 W/m2). fixed-4 has 19 lights, all out of frame, plus the in-frame Hemisphere and Core practicals. Its render settings are honest: both caustics on, clamp 0, filter_glossy 0. The shortcut-cut prop is last in the set, but its code and log are not in the folder, so I could not verify the cut. horn-card is still a reflection-only emitter (diffuse 0, shadow off, camera off, transmission off, ramped) whose measured effect in fixed-4 is nil on the horn. track-front1 is an honest head. It does what such a light does: cabinet front 15.4 -> 41.2, sill 7.4 -> 34.5. Its 14 deg spread lands more light than its 5 W/m2 label, so the cone (61.5) is brighter than in fixed-3 (56.8). ceiling-panel is honest in behaviour: right pillar +4, the wedge on the horn, bell +0.9. Its top edge, horn-card's, and the house and house-left discs' all pass through the 3.40 ceiling (by 0.18, 0.18, 0.61 and 0.59 m). Live's horn glow and cabinet glow were both tricks (bell 8.9 -> 0.3 and front 35.6 -> 15.4 once cut). At the site's sizes fixed-4 misreads the near Tropos: the woofer cone looks silver and the horn black with a triangle. Evidence is in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b62/critic-lights/: near-speaker.png, horn.png, cabinet-sill.png, site800-site-live-fixed4.png, thumb168-site-live-fixed4-x2.png, heat-fixed4-minus-fixed.png, heat-tiles-panel6-panel15-head6vs4.png, cores-zoom.png, tilemeas.txt, regions.txt, geom.txt.

verdicts.measurement: Bell box 1040,40-1320,240, L* for live / fixed / fixed-3 / fixed-4: 8.9 / 0.3 / 1.2 / 1.2. Pixels over L* 30: 7538 / 16 / 20 / 22. 99.5th percentile: 76.5 / 5.2 / 19.9 / 19.9. All reproduce. On the exact near-waveguide mask pixels (45,518 px), the mean is 11.0 live against 1.5 in fixed-4, and the median is 0.3 in every honest frame. Wedge box, measured on the coordinator's tiles: 0.0 / 3.6 / 8.7 with the panel at 0 / 6 / 15, and 5.2 in fixed-4. With no ceiling panel (horn-card on, transmission off) the bell reads 0.1. Seen in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b62/verify-lights/site800-site-live-fixed-fixed4.png, thumb-site-live-fixed4-x4.png (the real 168 x 94 size) and horn-plus3-2x-live-fixed-fixed4.png.
verdicts.reasoning: At 800 px and at the real 168 x 94 thumbnail, the fixed-4 horn is a black area with a neutral grey triangle outline pointing right. It reads as a graphic, not as a lemon horn. At +3 stops the triangle is hard-edged and untinted, as a reflection off the outer surface would be. The triangle comes from the panel: with the panel at 0 the horn is fully black. track-horn1 adds at most the 0.3 L* that fixed shows. The physics is honest: the horn is clear and stands in front of the niche's near-black felt (#1A1918, rough 0.95, planet_bar.py line 174), so honest light leaves it black. The fault is in how it reads, and at site sizes it misstates the Acid horn.

verdicts.measurement: Cone left-flank box, live / fixed / fixed-3 / fixed-4: 21.9 / 1.3 / 58.6 / 63.2 (reproduces). On exact masks of the near woofer: cone 26.4 (C* 17) / 5.8 / 56.9 / 60.9 (C* 3.9); dust cap 8.3 / 0.4 / 57.4 / 64.0. Lining beside the woofer in fixed-4 (my boxes x 1066-1092 and 1268-1296, y 400-560): 48.8 and 47.1. Amp box 73.7. Approved front-acid.png: cone ring 22.5 L* (p10-p90 about 10-34), cap 25.5, wall 89-93 (front-acid-cone-rings.png). Tiles: cone 65.6 with the panel at 0, 6 and 15 alike (head 10 W/m2, 22 deg). Head variants: 56.3 at 6 W/m2 / 22 deg, 64.1 at 6 W/m2 / 14 deg, 56.9 at 4 W/m2 / 14 deg. Seen in near-tropos-1to1-live-fixed-fixed4.png and in the thumbnail sheets.
verdicts.reasoning: The cone is a smooth, neutral light grey. At 1:1, at 800 px and at 168 px it reads as a metal (aluminium) cone, and it is the brightest large surface on the speaker. The head causes it: the cone reads the same whatever the panel's strength. The read inverts the product: in the approved front the cone is among the darkest parts, and here it outreads the white lining beside it. planet_bar.py line 136 records that the bay head was set steep on purpose to keep 'the cone in its cabinet's shade'. At the same 6 W/m2, narrowing the head from 22 to 14 degrees raised the cone from 56.3 to 64.1, so cutting watts alone will not fix it; the pool has to move off the cone. Like the critic, I could not check the cone material's albedo or gloss.

verdicts.measurement: fixed4.json horn-card: panel 1.4 x 0.9 m at (8.05, 4.9, 3.34), strength 10, diffuse 0.0, specular 1.0, transmission false, ramp 0.25-1-0.25 along x. lights.py panel(), lines 179-183: visible_camera False (no camera key), visible_shadow False, visible_transmission False when the spec says false, visible_diffuse = d >= 1 (False), visible_glossy = s >= 1 (True). The back face is a transparent BSDF. There are no twins, since the shares are 0 and 1. The no-panel tile is fixed2-10 with horn-card on: bell 0.1, wedge 0.0. My geometry check: 37.7 % of the card's area is above z 3.40.
verdicts.reasoning: Every flag the critic lists matches the code, and no real card behaves like that. On the horn its effect is nil. One correction: 'a few pixels at most' understates its reach. With visible_glossy on, plus reflective caustics and filter_glossy 0 in fixed-4, the card feeds every glossy lobe that faces it. It can also reach diffuse surfaces through any glossy bounce, for example off the glossy bar top. Its effect away from the horn is still unmeasured, so a fixed-5 without the card is the right test. It is a dishonest light with a small or unmeasured effect, so 'fix'.

verdicts.measurement: live.json horn-card has no transmission key, so panel() leaves it visible to transmission. It is also diffuse 0, camera off and shadow off. live render: caustics_reflective false and no filter_glossy key, so render.py line 282 gives blur_glossy = 0.5. Bell 8.9 -> 0.3; pixels over L* 30: 7538 -> 16 (the critic's 22 is fixed-4's count). Cabinet front box 35.6 -> 15.4; on the exact front-panel mask 43.3 -> 17.7. site-tropos-bar.webp differs from live.png by a mean of 3.2 levels and from fixed4.png by 13.7, so the site file is live. At +3 stops, live's glow is brightest mid-mouth and fades to the sides (horn-plus3-2x-live-fixed-fixed4.png).
verdicts.reasoning: The live horn's lemon glow has the card ramp's shape. It goes when the card's transmission visibility goes off, and the black felt behind the horn could not produce it. The shadow-ray shortcut is documented by README and gen.py (no_glass_shadows); the material code is not in the folder. Fixed changed four things at once, so the cabinet's fall from 35.6 to 15.4 cannot be put on the shortcut alone. In live, 'lights nothing' is loose wording: a card visible to transmission can reach whatever lies behind clear acrylic. Both tricks are in live, and they make the look of the near Tropos, so 'blocking'.

That is why it became 3 m. At house's own aim, a 3 m disc fits only with its centre at z <= 1.99 and y >= 0.52.
